merger_description:
Macmahon Holdings Ltd (**Macmahon**) proposes to acquire 100% of the issued share capital of Aspect Engineering Solutions Pty Ltd and its wholly owned subsidiaries, including View Resources Pty Ltd and Aspect Vietnam Limited Liability Company (together, **Aspect**) (the **Acquisition**).

Macmahon is an ASX-listed diversified contracting company, which services major resource companies across various commodity sectors. It provides surface and underground mining, and civil construction and infrastructure services to resources projects across Australia and Southeast Asia. Macmahon’s services encompass mine development and materials delivery through to engineering, civil construction, on-site mining services, rehabilitation, site remediation, training and equipment maintenance, and refurbishment services.

In 2024, Macmahon acquired Decmil Group Ltd (now Decmil Group Pty Ltd) (**Decmil**). Decmil is the civil infrastructure construction business of Macmahon. It provides engineering, construction and maintenance services for projects in the resources, infrastructure and energy sectors. Decmil focuses on large civil construction and non-process infrastructure projects.

Aspect provides multi-disciplinary engineering, project delivery, professional services and operations and maintenance services. It primarily services gold, lithium and critical minerals clients in Western Australia.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition, given:
a. there is limited horizontal overlap between Macmahon
(through Decmil) and Aspect in the supply of engineering
consultancy services and engineering construction services
in Western Australia and Australia
b. the parties’ combined share of engineering consultancy
services and engineering construction services in Western
Australia and Australia is estimated to be low and the
increment arising from the Acquisition is expected to be
small
c. there are alternative suppliers of engineering consultancy
services and engineering construction services in Western
Australia and Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
